chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

I read in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) wrote a document between the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who joined them from the people of Yathrib:

that every raiding party which fights must do so in a manner where they take turns according to proper conduct and equity among the Muslims — for no war is permissible except with the permission of those responsible for it;
and that the neighbor is like oneself, without causing harm or committing sin; and the sanctity of the neighbor upon the neighbor is like the sanctity of his own mother and his own father.
No believer should make peace apart from another believer during fighting in the way of God, except on the basis of justice and equality.

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: Ansar — the Helpers, Medinans who welcomed the migrants
key_terms.الْجَارَ كَالنَّفْسِ: The neighbor is like oneself — a foundational principle of neighborly sanctity
key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرِينَ: Muhajirun — the Emigrants from Mecca to Medina
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: The way of God — fighting or striving in God's cause
key_terms.عَدْلٍ وَسَوَاءٍ: Justice and equality — conditions for a legitimate peace settlement
key_terms.يَثْرِبَ: Yathrib — the pre-Islamic name for Medina

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad write in the Constitution of Medina about neighbors and warfare?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a passage from the Book of Ali (AS), which recorded a foundational constitutional document (known historically as the Sahifat al-Madinah or Constitution of Medina) written by the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) shortly after the Hijra. The document established binding principles among the Muhajirun and Ansar: that military campaigns must be conducted with fairness; that no war is valid without legitimate authority; that neighbors must be treated with the same care as oneself, without harm or sin; and that no Muslim may conclude a separate peace during jihad without collective justice and equality. The original audience — the first generation of Muslims in Medina — understood this document as the foundational law of the new Muslim community, establishing both military ethics and the sacred inviolability of neighborly relations.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his father<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘I<sup>asws</sup> read in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> wrote an ordinance between the Emigrants and the Helpers and the one who attaches with them from the people of Yasrab that:
‘Every combatant who combats must be with step by step with the enjoining of the good and the equity between the Muslims, for a war is not allowed except by the permission of its rightful ones,
and that the neighbour is like the self without harm and sin; and the sanctitiy of the neighbour upon the neighbour is like the sanctity of his own mother and his own father.
No Believer should make peace besides a Believer during the fighting in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> except upon justice and equality’.
en.sarwar: Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that he has read in the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, wrote the following in a letter for al-Muhajirun, al- Ansar and those who join them from the people of Yathrib: ‘Every mobilization that is arranged for an armed confrontation must be continued step by step with legitimacy and justice among the Muslims.
It is not permissible to start a war without the permission of the people (who will maintain it).
The rights of neighbors are just like one’s soul that must be held harmless and sinless. The respect and honor of a neighbor is like the honor and respect of a mother and father.
A believing person does not make peace just for himself, ignoring the other believer during a war for the cause of Allah, except on the basis of justice and equality.’”
